# Notes On Our Q3 Hiring Process Changes

Let me be clear. Recruiting has been rough this year.

The part everyone misses is that the bottleneck was never the top of the funnel. It's not a sourcing problem. It's a scheduling problem. We had plenty of candidates. We could not get them in front of anyone.

Think about it: how many good engineers have you lost to a two-week gap between screens? Too many. That's the whole story.

So we decided to embark on a rebuild of the coordinator flow and harness a paradigm shift in how we book panels. Cutting-edge stuff. The thing that actually fixed it: one shared calendar.

Our recruiter drops the request. The coordinator picks a slot. The scheduler sends the invite. Many argue that automation is paramount here, and industry reports suggest that companies who empower their talent teams see better outcomes, solidifying their position as employers of choice.

The new flow gives our team the ability to book a panel in under a day. It has genuinely improved candidate experience across the board. Worth sitting with that for a second.

Time-to-schedule dropped from 11 days to 1.4 days over 63 open roles between July and September. Offer acceptance went from 58% to 71%.

Honestly? I pushed back on this project for two months because I thought it was busywork, and I was flat wrong about that. Rachel called it before any of us did. Credit where it's due.

The rollout was inevitably a bit messy. Two panels got double-booked in week one. We fixed it.

Overall, this quarter's changes reflect a multifaceted commitment to hiring excellence, underscoring the value we place on every candidate. Hiring isn't a funnel. It's a conversation.
